To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of intraoperative neuromonitoring can help identify a rare but serious complication of anterior spinal fusion, which can result in permanent neurologic injury.
the combination of peripheral and central SSEPs with pulse oximetry can provide a sensitive and reliable method for the intraoperative detection and prevention of vascular insults to the spinal cord.

(1) intraoperative spinal cord evoked potential monitoring using peripheral nerve stimulation can be used to identify ischemia of spinal cord due to occlusion of the common iliac artery; (2) the ischemia was detected before the onset of motor deficits; and (3) early recognition of ischemia allowed for successful revascularization of the spinal cord and prevented neurological sequelae.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method for the detection of the neural pathways in the human body.
the use of intraoperative monitoring to prevent vascular complications in anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF).
the detection of thrombotic occlusions of the iliac bifurcation during anterior lumbar interbody fusions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of intraoperative SSEP monitoring for spinal procedures is not only safe but also cost-effective and beneficial.
the use of cortical SSEPs alone for monitoring of spinal cord function is not recommended.
intraoperative monitoring using SSEPs at the peripheral and cortical levels is an essential tool in detecting vascular insults to the spinal cord during anterior lumbar interbody fusion surgery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
intraoperative neuromonitoring can be used to detect vascular insults and can be used in conjunction with other monitoring modalities to provide a more comprehensive picture of spinal cord function.
intraoperative monitoring using SSEPs is a valuable tool to prevent ischemic insult and to detect acute and delayed vascular insults during spinal surgery.
a multimodal approach using peripheral and cortical SSEPs is the most reliable method for monitoring the neural pathway during spinal reconstructive surgery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intraoperative monitoring with cortical SSEPs alone may not detect ischemic insult due the iliac arteries and that peripheral SSEPs may be more sensitive for the detection of such insults.
a multimodal monitoring approach is essential in the prevention of ischemic insults to the spinal cord during spinal reconstructive surgery.
the combination of peripheral and cortical SSEPs can be used for the early detection of ischemic insult.
